Loaded Accessibility Review

I recreated three pages from Loaded in Figma and marked specific places where shoppers could run into accessibility barriers.

Design focus Document where a barrier might occur and what to check in the browser.

PROJECT CONTEXT

Project and approach

I followed the shopping flow from the homepage to a product page and into checkout. I wanted each note to point to something a teammate could find on the screen, so I used lettered markers tied to a shared legend.

01 / DESIGN DECISIONS

Tie each concern to a specific element

On each page I looked at contrast, alternative text, visible keyboard focus, form labels, and heading hierarchy. The shared legend makes it possible to find a concern and compare how the same type of element is handled elsewhere in the flow.

02 / DESIGN DECISIONS

Start the browser checks at checkout

At checkout, a shopper needs to know what each field asks for and which control has focus. I marked those elements in the reconstruction so I could return to the corresponding page and check how the form actually behaves with a keyboard.

REFLECTION

What I learned and what I’d test next

The annotated screens give a design or engineering teammate a place to start. I’d follow up in the browser by measuring contrast, checking headings and text alternatives, and navigating checkout using only a keyboard. Then I could turn any confirmed barriers into specific fixes and retest them.
